newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-MARKGRAAFF WORRIED ABOUT INJURIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MARKGRAAFF WORRIED ABOUT INJURIES.

text.p: Springbok coach Andre Markgraaff is worried that a bruising Currie Cup final at Ellis Park this Saturday might result in injuries to some of the key players in his 36-man national squad, particularly flyhalf Henry Honiball.

Speaking after a training session at Loftus Versfeld on Monday for his likely mid-week team on tour to Argentina, France and Wales, Markgraaff admitted he was a little wary about the Transvaal/Natal encounter.

"I'll be keeping my eye on the two number 10s very closely because they are key players - particularly Henry Honiball. He is struggling with his hamstring and I'm worried that he might get injured here," Markgraaff said at a news conference.

"I think we saw the difference that he makes to the Natal team on Saturday. If he had played (in the semi-final against Free State), I think it might have been the difference between them (Natal) scoring 35 and 65 points. But even if he doesn't play on Saturday, that certainly won't rule him out of the tour."
Markgraaff said the only worries in his squad were lock Krynauw Otto (head cold) and fullback Theo van Rensburg (leg injury).
"But both should come right in the next few days," he said.
Markgraaff said it was possible the mid-week Springbok team on tour might play an extra fixture in Wales.
"At the moment, they are without a match for the last 12 days or so of our tour and the tour management is looking at the possibility of an extra fixture. But nothing has been confirmed yet."
